utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Good morning, Mr. Erdemovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Erdemovic.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you for pausing between question and answer. We do tend to forget this. I wanted to move on and to look at some of the other details. They would take ten people out of the bus at a time and people were shot in groups of ten; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who would take them out?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, there was the escort with the driver in the first bus. As far as I can remember, there were two military policemen and they would take them out of the buses. In the first bus there was Brano Gojkovic and Golijan Vlastimir and they escorted them to the site at which they were executed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you said that the drivers were amazed and they were convinced that these people were there for the purposes of an exchange. And do you stand by that claim?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only remember the first driver, but I can't really remember what the situation was with the other drivers because I didn't have contact with all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You heard the first driver say that he was convinced that they were being taken for an exchange and he was amazed at what was happening; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, and Brano Gojkovic also ordered one of the drivers to take a rifle and open fire to a group of Muslims because he didn't want to have any witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Which driver are you referring to? Which bus?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's try and understand what was happening at that site.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see P4308, page 222. And could the usher help Mr. Erdemovic to use the electronic pen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you like to upload already marked by the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Excellency. It's new. Could this central part be enlarged? Could we zoom in to the part where we can see both roads and the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, what is this area here where these executions took place?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assumed that it was a farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the ground like? What was the ground like? What was the earth like in the field where the execution was carried out?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What did you have there, grass or other kinds of plants? What was there?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there was some corn there that had been harvested. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you take the electronic pen now and mark the route that these people used to reach a certain site, and could you mark the site. Could you also mark the site where the bus was.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now use these dots -- yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I need to understand the point of this exercise. He did this in his chief -- examination-in-chief, so you are -- you wanted to check whether he did -- he does the same, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Excellency. No, no. I want a new spatial and temporal framework to be established so that we can understand what actually happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please use the colour red now and could you show how they were lined up by symbolising this with ten red dots. I'm referring to the first ten.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In one line or in two lines?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In one line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you use the blue pen to mark the site at which the eight of you were located?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How many metres were you away from them?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say what the distance was exactly, how many metres there were between us, because we weren't far away from them, from their backs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So they had their backs turned towards you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So what was the purpose of blindfolding them in that case?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They already had these blindfolds on in the buses, and as I have already testified, as far as I can remember, in the first bus their hands were tied behind their backs. I don't know who took this decision and why it was decided that they should be blindfolded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And this entire route that you have marked is a route that they covered with these blindfolds on. Does that concern the first ten of them or the whole bus?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the buses that arrived there. On that day, all the buses that arrived at the farm on that day, all the people from the buses were taken down the route that I have marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And were only the first ten blindfolded and had their hands tied or did that concern all 50 of them from the first bus?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, they were all blindfolded and they all had their hands tied, at least those from the first bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid that we still need the usher's assistance. Could you please mark the site at which the other group of ten was located?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. With regard to the first bus, could you mark the place -- could you first mark the place where the first group of ten was located and then the next four groups.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if I can mark all of that, but as I have already testified, the first group was here and then we went back towards the farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you mark the field where the bodies were, the body-strewn field.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How big is that area, is that field? 15 by 15 metres or 20 by 20 metres, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I can't remember the size of the area. I really wasn't that interested in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. So you dealt with one bus. How much time did it take for these five groups of ten to come out of the first bus?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, there are two issues here: What happened and then there's the issue of numbers. You want to say that 1.000 to 1.200 people were killed here, and that they all came in groups of ten down this route from 11.00 to 2.00 or 3.00, and you said they were all taken to the field that you have marked. Mr. Erdemovic, a man who is killed and who is on the ground takes up an area of 3 to 4 square metres. Would you agree that it's bad enough to kill one person, why should we exaggerate the numbers now? So why is what you are saying so difficult to believe?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Well, Dr. Karadzic, I mean, that's a comment and not a question in reality. You've also made the assertion as if it's established in evidence that a man who is killed and is on the ground takes up an area of 3 to 4 square metres. There doesn't seem to be any evidential basis for that whatsoever. Again, these are multiple questions. You're descending into detail that it's difficult to see the relevance of. Either you are contesting the core of this witness's evidence or you're not. And at the moment, with your time rapidly running out, it seems to me at least that you've got a long way to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I thank Judge Morrison, but you are not giving evidence. Just put one question at a time and do not make statements.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, do we agree that between the parking and the execution site, the distance is between 80 and 100 metres?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say exactly what the distance is, but I think that is correct. Perhaps the distance would be between a hundred and 200 metres, but I can't say exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. And how long does it take to take ten blindfolded individuals from the bus to the execution site?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I have already answered your question. It wasn't possible for me to follow all of this and keep an eye on my watch to see how long it took to take them from that place to the site of execution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And the eight of you opened fire on the ten of them; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I opened fire on the person in front of me, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So if you opened fire on the person in front of you, then you killed five individuals from that bus; isn't that correct? If there were five groups of ten, then you killed five of them from that bus; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I didn't count the number of people I killed. I can't answer that question. If you think I killed five of them, well, that is your opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. So you are trying to say that after 11.00 and up until 2.00 or 3.00, so many people were executed applying this rhythm, if you will?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never said that this was an exact figure. I always said it was an estimate. Maybe I said -- well, maybe I increased the number, but that was my thinking at that point in time because this went on for a long time for me. For me, it was an eternity, everything that happened on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So now you're saying that you don't know the number and that you probably increased it, exaggerated it; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, he answered the question. That's your statement, Mr. Karadzic. Yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, I also just wanted to note, this is the second time Mr. Karadzic has said the time was 11.00 until 2.00 or 3.00. If you look at transcript page 10972, Mr. Erdemovic's Popovic testimony, he actually says he supposes from 10.00 until 3.00 or 4.00. So perhaps that -- when Mr. Karadzic is citing the times he could be accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. "I suppose from 10.00 until 3.00 or 4.00. I can't tell you exactly." Yes. Thank you, Mr. Mitchell. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But, Your Excellency, yesterday we realised that they could not have arrived by 10.00. We worked out this entire timetable, when they got up, when they had breakfast, et cetera. So yesterday we established that Mr. Erdemovic actually said that they arrived around 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't know who established that. Put your question to the witness now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the witness, yesterday he confirmed that it was 11.00 and that there weren't any prisoners there, and the prisoners arrived only after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, did you receive any information to the effect that there was some grave there already, that some people had already been buried there?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person that remained at that farm when the lieutenant-colonel left -- actually, before the first execution started, after it was all over I cannot tell you exactly what time it was in the afternoon. This person said that some people had been executed there earlier on. He did not say when this "earlier on" was when this actually happened. I cannot confirm that, but that is what that individual had said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But the person did not say that they had been executed. That person said that there had been burials there earlier on; right? Look at this interview with Ruez, the one that you had. 1D5051 [as interpreted]. Could you please put the date there and sign that, what you have there in front of you.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know where they were buried? Can you mark that as well, if you know. 1D5150. But, tell me, do you know where they were buried? Can you mark the place where they were buried? Was a grave there when you arrived? Had it already been dug?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no grave there, nothing had been dug. That person from the farm just said that roughly around that place where these persons from Srebrenica had been killed, there had been people buried there too. I really cannot explain any of this, why that happened. He did not show this to me exactly, where it was that these persons had been buried.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D2134, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D5150, please. In Serbian page 25, in English 38. 1D5150. Serbian page 25, English 38. Serbian 25, English 38.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember having spoken to Mr. Ruez, an investigator?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. I talked to Mr. Ruez quite a few times.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] English page 38, please -- actually, maybe it's 38 in e-court. I'm not sure it's the same. Could you please -- actually, can we zoom in in the Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And can you read your first answer and the first question that was put to you. Can you read it out loud, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "We received information that allegedly a guard said that in that area there is a mass grave from the time of the Second World War. Have you heard anything about this?"

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Your answer?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "No. Look, I did hear about this but it's not from the Second World War. It was said -- well, I don't know. He did not say from the Second World War. He said that some people had already been buried there. Now I don't know which people. That's what he said when he said that these people would be buried there."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you did not notice a freshly dug grave. And he said to you that some people had been buried there; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not that he said that to me. I mean, I cannot remember who it was that he was talking to, but I was there when he spoke about that and that's why I heard that. It's not that I asked him any questions, which people, where's the grave? I wasn't interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just repeated what it was that he had said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Erdemovic, how did things develop then? Who did you talk to about this and who did you not tell about this?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean? What do you mean to whom did I talk and with whom was I silent?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who did you hide this from?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not discuss that event with my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And who else? Did you talk to everyone else about that? Who else did you tell this to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, what do you mean by "this"? Be specific in putting your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: A horrific thing happened, one that leaves quite an impression. And I'm interested in hearing who you told about this, Mr. Erdemovic, and who you did not reveal this to.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I talked to persons who I thought would not tell Pelemis because we were not supposed to talk about our actions. I talked to persons I trusted. I talked to persons I had confidence in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Apart from these eight persons, did you dare talk to anyone else? Did you talk to anyone else, apart from these eight persons?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, on the 16th we returned to Vlasenica, and then from Vlasenica we went to Bijeljina. As for these eight men, I just saw one of them in Bijeljina. I did not see the other six.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You never saw them again?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw them perhaps three or four months later, the persons from Vlasenica, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, why did this quarrel break out in the cafe in Bijeljina, the one that was followed by a shoot-out?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you say "Bijeljina," Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, this coffee bar or cafe where there was this shoot-out, is that in Bijeljina, in your view?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Why did this quarrel break out? Why was there a shooting?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That evening, before the shooting, I was with Mr. Kremenovic and perhaps two other persons, I cannot remember exactly, from my unit. I think that one of them -- one of them was Golijan, I think Zijad Zigic, and there were other people there too, but I cannot remember now. I talked to Mr. Kremenovic about what had happened and what we had been asked to do. Mr. Pelemis - how do I put this? How do I explain this to you? - he was taking advantage of us for his own purposes. After that we talked some more and went to this cafe in Bijeljina. We were all under the influence. Around midnight, I cannot remember exactly, Stanko Savanovic -- well, there was this complication, quarrel, Savanovic took his gun out and started shooting at me, Mr. Kremenovic and Zijad Zigic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. First of all, let's clarify this, Zijad Zigic, he's a member of your unit and he's a Muslim; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Why did this quarrel break out? When -- when were guns drawn -- or actually after what particular subject, after which words?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I already talked about the subject, it was Pelemis and his orders and taking advantage of persons from the unit for his own purposes. After that, as I've already said, what happened happened in that coffee bar. I cannot remember anymore. I think Savanovic did something, he either broke a glass or something. I know that this turned out to be very complicated. Zijad Zigic and Savanovic quarrelled and then he took a gun out and started shooting at us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the discussion in that cafe was about who profited financially from your actions and who did not, and was the dispute on account of who fared better and who fared worse?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That did not start in the cafe. We first brought that subject up -- well, as I've already said, we were saying that Mr. Pelemis is using persons from our unit for his own purposes. That started even before we arrived in the cafe, and it wasn't that this discussion took place only that evening. It went on after that evening and started before that evening. So Mr. Kremenovic, who was a lieutenant in the Army of Republika Srpska, he was the deputy of 2nd Lieutenant Milorad Pelemis, I don't know why, and then after that night he was removed from the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Kremenovic was removed from the unit after that night; right? And then after that -- actually, it's the same -- is that the same Kremenovic who had agreed with you that you should talk to journalists?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And who removed Kremenovic from the unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as Kremenovic said -- I mean, I don't know. I was seriously wounded that night in that cafe. And I spent a month, I think, at the military hospital in Belgrade. So when I spoke to Kremenovic again, he said that Pelemis decided to remove him from the unit. Now, I don't know whether that was just Pelemis's decision or did it come from a higher command; that I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And is it correct that Franc Kos, a Slovene, was a member of your unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And is it correct that Franc Kos had some authority over that part of the detachment in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was platoon leader.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that Franc Kos in that capacity removed Kremenovic because he was an adventurist?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer, Mr. Karadzic. As I've already said, I was in hospital, and what happened and who removed Kremenovic, that is something that I cannot give an answer to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And is it correct -- or, rather, could you tell us who fared well in material terms and who didn't fare so well. And this was the reason for discontent. Were you one of those who did well or were you one of those who didn't gain any advantage from the affair?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, it's not a matter of who fared well and who didn't. What was at stake is the fact that Mr. Pelemis, our unit's commander, took advantage of us. He used us for purposes that didn't fall under the mandate of our unit, so to speak, and he enriched himself by ordering us to do certain things. And if you want to call it a quarrel, this is why this quarrel broke out that evening. And even before that evening and afterwards we continued to discuss this matter in our unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How was it possible for Pelemis to become rich?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How was he able to become rich, well, that wasn't the only problem, Mr. Karadzic. I had problems with Mr. Pelemis even before the 10th Sabotage Platoon was officially established. That was because of some of his orders and because he didn't trust me, and so on and so forth, and because he made certain requests from people. He was a selfish person and no one meant anything to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But he did accept you as a member of the 10th Sabotage Detachment, although you had a misunderstanding even before that. But let's leave that. We're now going to focus on the events after the Branjevo Farm. If there was a quarrel, some were for and some were against. Who was accused of having fared well and who made these accusations?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember having discussed who fared well in material terms. All we knew was that Pelemis - I can't find my words now - he took advantage of the unit and of all of us for his own benefit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Mr. Erdemovic, you said several times that Mr. Pelemis took advantage of you. He used you for purposes that didn't fall under the mandate of our unit. So could you give us examples of Pelemis taking advantage of you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1995, at the beginning of 1995, I was the commander of a group that had been designated to go and attempt to capture a counter-intelligence officer from the ABiH, either to capture him or to place a bomb under his car. When we went down there, we were provided with information on the road where this was to be done. When we arrived there, I, Franc Kos, and the others noticed that civilians would be at risk at the site because it was an inhabited area, civilians inhabited that area. We carried out reconnaissance for about one day. We tried to see what could be done. We tried to see how it would be safest to proceed. And having carried out this reconnaissance, we decided to return, not to carry out the task. That was after one day down there. When we returned, since I was the group commander, Mr. Pelemis and Salapura arrived at the barracks on that day. And he told me that I was lying. They said that they had information that the place wasn't an inhabited place and that even if a civilian were to be killed, it didn't matter. And there was another matter, there were various sponsors or people who would give him donations, money, so that he could spend money. He continually went to Belgrade to have a good time. He would go to spend time in hotels and so on and so forth. The last case that occurred had to do with Srebrenica. I don't know exactly whether this, in fact, happened, but there were rumours in Bijeljina according to which Mr. Pelemis had received I don't know how many kilos of gold that had been found in Srebrenica, and that's why he sent us there to shoot these civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So there was a quarrel about who was doing well and who wasn't and there was a quarrel that had to do with why you hadn't received some of the gold. Some people were unhappy about this situation; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, it wasn't just a matter of who had received certain things and who hadn't because we were asked to do things that we did not agree with. And what was even worse -- that was even worse for us because Mr. Pelemis was using us for his own purposes, for his own benefit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So Pelemis didn't ask you to do this and you weren't informed of the task by Pelemis; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which task you are referring to, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The task that involved killing these people. You heard nothing about this from Pelemis; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whenever we had to carry out tasks -- well, Mr. Pelemis knew all the tasks. I didn't hear anything about it that morning from Pelemis, but he should have known about that because we wouldn't have been allowed to go and carry out the task without his knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And did you volunteer to carry out the task? Did the eight of you volunteer?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have a look at 1D5158 in the e-court system.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that this is a memorandum, an official note, on the conversation or an interview, rather, with Mr. Kos.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have a look at the second page, please. Could we zoom in to the lower part where it says: [In English] "In 1995 (months of May and June) the 10th Sabotage Detachment together with the Drina Wolves unit took part in the assault on Srebrenica and in conquering it. On 16th of July he received a phone call by Major Dragomir Pecanac and was given the order of designating 7 soldiers in order to ensure protection of transport at the place of the deserted beef farm at Pilica, Municipality of Zvornik. The group designated by Mr. Kos was voluntarily joined by Erdemovic."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Your officer says that you joined voluntarily?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see what he says, and to be quite frank, he's lying. I didn't want to say that, but he's lying.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Erdemovic, I can tell you that he's not the only person that says that you joined voluntarily. Another witness said something to that effect here. But now let us see how this issue of the gold cropped up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like a cite for that last statement. If he's referring to Mr. Todorovic and the quote that I read out yesterday, I don't think that was about whether he joined voluntarily.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps it's not that quote, but I do believe that it is that witness who said that Erdemovic joined voluntarily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, that exact -- the section that I was referring to says Erdemovic said he was forced to do something at gunpoint. It didn't get into -- or my reading of it is it's not referring to whether he volunteered at Vlasenica to join the unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't you leave it at that. Let's proceed. Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. Just one minute, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, who signed for the issuing of equipment on the 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I answered the question yesterday. I can't remember who signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on to another subject. Mr. Erdemovic, yesterday we listened [as interpreted] to a document and saw a document that was prepared for you. As you're not of Serbian origin, they gave you ID cards with other names. Were these names supposed to be similar to Serbian names, to look like Serbian names?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So does that mean that while you were in the unit, you did not have to show identity cards of any kind, and this measure was taken for purposes of demobilisation, when you as civilians would be subjected to controls?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was in the barracks in Bijeljina, we all had these military cards which stated the unit you were a member of and your first and last name. We had these IDs, but as to why these identity cards were made, I don't know. All I know is that I read that they had been made because the Hague Tribunal was interested in the eight of us, the eight of us who were not of Serbian ethnicity in that unit. However, the date was the 16th of January, 1996. And when I arrived in The Hague in March or April of that year, they knew nothing about me or other members from my unit. So when I saw that document, I was surprised.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, who from your group went to fight as a mercenary in Zaire?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer that, but while I was in the Detention Unit in The Hague, I read certain articles which stated that some individuals from the 10th Sabotage Detachment went to Zaire. I was in The Hague Detention Unit then, so I can't answer your question precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could these false ID cards also be used for those purposes, or rather, did you hear the names or about the names under which they went to Zaire, the names they used when they went to Zaire?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, as I have already said, I was in the Detention Unit in Scheveningen. I had absolutely no contact with men from my unit. All I have told you is information that I obtained from the newspapers. I know nothing else about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Mr. Mitchell, I checked the transcript of Mr. Todorovic. It's 7th of February, transcript page 24204, line 19 to line 21. "Q. Was Drazen Erdemovic there? "A. Erdemovic was with me in Trebinje but he volunteered. He was not forced to go." That's what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I accept that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know which country and the secret service of which country organised your colleagues going to Zaire?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly which country organised this. I just know that I read in this article that these were individuals from the 10th Sabotage Detachment. I think there was some lieutenant-colonel or something like that from some French army or -- I don't know. I cannot remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let us move on to another topic, Mr. Erdemovic. You said that it was possible to take personal revenge and you mentioned a man who killed 250 prisoners to avenge his brother; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've already said what it was that he was saying. I don't know how many persons he killed. I know what he was bragging about. I cannot tell you why he did that. I mean, I just repeated his words.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But he did mention that his brother had lost his life and that he did all of that for his brother; right?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Further on you said that when the men from Bratunac came for the liquidation of the people from the last bus, that some people were recognised and mistreated and beaten; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall the video footage where you recognised a man wearing a US army uniform and jeans who was killed? According to you, was he killed on the 11th of July when you were in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But do you know, Mr. Erdemovic, that that footage was filmed on the 13th of July and that in that case that body would probably be decayed, in view of the fact that it was July, and that the entire town would be stinking, there would be stench in the entire town?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I really can't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, you refused to tell the Court the name of one of the people in the photo because you said he hadn't done anything wrong and that you were on good terms with him; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before that answer. Yes, is it related to that video, Mr. Mitchell?

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: It is, Mr. President. That video is of 12 July 1995, and the reference for that is in the source material at the back of the trial video book. It lists the dates of each sequence, and that was the very first sequence in part 2 in that book, that's ERN 07048028. And it's the sequence from 10 seconds to 1 minute and 14 seconds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Who was it taken by?

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'll have to get back to you on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: It was seized from a search of Darko Mladic's house in 2009, but the identity of the actual cameraman I'm not sure of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic. If you do not agree with Mr. Mitchell's intervention, that it was taken on 12th of July, you need to give the reference.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, thank you. Perhaps after the break. I'm not sure if I can dispute that, in fact, because I know that Mr. Pirocanac was the one who filmed that, Zoran Petrovic, namely, and I thought that that was part of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It is true, isn't it, that there is a man from Vlasenica in the photo there and you didn't want to mention his name because he was on good terms with you; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's not just that we were on good terms. I know that that person didn't do anything wrong; and secondly, when I testified in Popovic, Mr. Ostojic - and I can't quite recall the detail - but Mr. Ostojic, the attorney, the Defence counsel, said that he wanted to have the name of that person. And then I did say the name in private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, was there anyone that you were not on good terms with in your detachment?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, who was it that I wasn't on good terms in my detachment? Well, I think I've already said that a number of times. The greatest problems that I had were with Mr. Pelemis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could the Chamber move into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, did you try, for those reasons of personal animosity against Mr. Pelemis, to involve him in some criminal offence or crime at all costs?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us yesterday that this unit was an elite unit and that it had a very good reputation up until the 16th of July; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that for the Bijeljina platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what you saw on the 11th in Srebrenica, was that -- did that come as a shock to you, that this prisoner would be shot, shot dead?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, of course it was unpleasant because that person actually had his throat slit. He was slaughtered with a knife. Now, secondly, Mr. Pelemis, before we set out into town, he said that we should not open fire on civilians. But about an hour or an hour and a half later, he ordered Zoran Maljic to slit the throat of that man. I just could not understand that. I had heard stories about such incidents earlier on in Vlasenica and Zvornik, I can't tell you exactly, but I did hear stories like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, on another occasion, did you attribute this same or similar thing to Mr. Pelemis where it involved a completely different location; and then after you saw the footage, then you said that it was in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't recall that I said anything like that, that I would have said that it was someplace else and then later that it was, in fact, in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, you said that Mr. Pelemis took a man, a Muslim, out of a prison and that he had him killed. This is what you said in your earlier statements, and then after you saw this footage, then you said that he had killed this man wearing that American jacket. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, as for that person who was taken out of detention in Vlasenica, that event was after Srebrenica, when Pelemis had that accident with a UN APC. And then a person from the Vlasenica platoon was late catching a bus for Srebrenica, and then when we returned to Vlasenica the night of the 12th, Major Pecanac was there and they decided that that person who had been late for Srebrenica, that he would be charged with killing that man. I did not attribute that to Mr. Pelemis. I said that Pecanac was involved in this, as far as I can recall. As for this man in Srebrenica whose throat had been slit by Zoran Maljic, I know for certain that that was ordered by Pelemis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Before the break, let's talk a little bit about your background and your career. Could you answer with yes or no, please. Is it true that you completed your regular military service, in JNA, in 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you then observed that Muslims mobilised their men, Serbs mobilised their own people, and Croats their own, and at that point you didn't want to join any army but then you decided to join the BH army?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. While you were a member of the BH army, you helped Serbs from Tuzla who wanted to cross over to Republika Srpska to go across the separation line. Was that indeed the case and did Serbs very much want to leave Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not help Serbs while I was in the BH army. I started helping Serbs while -- when I was in the HVO, in the military police. As for the Serbs from Tuzla, I don't know exactly how that went, but as for -- I was in Tuzla, or nearby, and people who lived in that area, they wanted to leave and go to the area that was held by the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that there were exchanges going on and that Muslims were leaving Bijeljina, whereas Serbs were going to Bijeljina? So are you aware that this was a two-way street, as it were?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I know that people were transported from Republika Srpska to the area that belonged to the BH army, and I also know that people of Serb ethnicity who were in Bosnia-Herzegovina were transported to Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that there were all kinds of attorneys on both sides who compiled lists and actually charged people when transferring them to other areas in order to re-unite them with their families? Did you hear of this term, "family reunion"?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I don't know anything about any attorneys or lawyers. I was not present when these exchanges occurred, and as for the term, I don't know anything about it so I can't answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But do you know that this had to be paid for, that it cost some money, that it had to -- that these transfers from either side across the line cost some money?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't. I don't know anything about that. I cannot give you a precise answer to that question, but I do know that some people did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you profit in any way from this, from transferring Serbs?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When you testified in Tolimir, on page 1899 of the transcript, didn't you say that you were given fuel that was scarce at the time, that the Serbs would give you fuel?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the fuel that I got from the Serbs was not for my personal profit. This was just to be used so that I can transport these people to the separation line. So I used the fuel to transport these people to the separation line.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After all of these misunderstandings, after the BH army you joined the HVO; and then the HVO arrested you because of these activities and handed you over to the BH army. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After this you managed to cross over into Republika Srpska; correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After that, you reported to the military office, and they -- and you were told there that there was an ethnically mixed unit and that it would be best if you joined it; and then you volunteered to join that unit. Correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I crossed over to Republika Srpska, I did not join the army immediately. I went to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia because I received threats when I moved to Republika Srpska. However, I arrived in Republika Srpska in November 1993, I believe, and then I left for the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia because I did not want to join any army. Now, in 1994, in early 1994, there were mobilisations in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia of able-bodied men who came from Bosnia and Herzegovina. So what happened was they would stop you on the road, on the street, and they would ask for your ID. And if you had an ID that was issued in Bosnia and Herzegovina, they would take you to a barracks where you would be issued a uniform and sent back to Bosnia and Herzegovina. So I decided to return to Republika Srpska, together with my wife. We went to a place called Miljevina which was near Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were not arrested in that way and deported. You came on your own; right? You thought that that was wiser?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not that I thought it was wiser. I thought that I had no other choice, and indeed I did not have any other choice.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was that unit your choice? Did you join it voluntarily? Did you decide to join that unit, this platoon that was later on transformed into the 10th Sabotage Detachment?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That unit included a few Croats, a Slovene, and a Muslim. That's why I made that decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Erdemovic, you made different statements, you gave different statements to journalists. Is it true that you misrepresented certain things, especially as far as dates are concerned?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I talked to a lady journalist from the ABC, I said that we went to Srebrenica on the 16th. I said that because Kremenovic had said to me that if something happened, the dates should not tally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. That's what you did when you spoke to the lady journalist, but what did you say before the Serb authorities, the authorities in Belgrade? Did you keep silent about something when you spoke to them or did you deceive them?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The night before we were arrested, we received a telephone call from this lady journalist. She said to us that this cassette with my statement disappeared from Belgrade airport and that she had been searched at the airport and interrogated and whatever. I wasn't the person talking to her, it was Kremenovic. Then I decided to repeat that because I assumed that they already had all of that on that recording, and I decided to repeat that story to the court in Belgrade. Also, I said that I wanted to go to The Hague and to tell everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, please, in Belgrade were you in detention? Were criminal charges brought against you; and if so, what were these charges exactly?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was detained during the first two days, as far as I can remember, in Novi Sad. Then I appeared before a court in Novi Sad. I cannot tell you exactly what -- I cannot give you an exact answer. I cannot tell you exactly what was written there in those criminal charges or whatever. Then I was transferred to Belgrade, to some house, where there were state security officials, officials from the State Security Service of Serbia. And then I stayed there, I cannot remember exactly, perhaps a month; and then I was transferred to The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What was it that you were suspected of? How did they qualify that? War crime? Murder? What?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: War crime. I cannot remember exactly now. I think it was war crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you ever charged with genocide, Mr. Erdemovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember, Mr. Karadzic. Can you show some paper to me or something? Then I can answer. I cannot recall because ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you confess having committed genocide?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Karadzic, I cannot. If you have some evidence, please show it to me because I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's do it this way. Were the negotiations with the Prosecution difficult? And were you interested in reaching an agreement with the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, when I was transferred from Belgrade to The Hague, the Prosecution informed me straight away that they could make no promises to me, that they did not want to promise me anything, that I was there because I wanted to be there and to tell them my story. No one made any promises to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you keenly interested in reaching this agreement?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My Defence attorney spoke to the Prosecution about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Tell us, did you give an interview to "Le Figaro"?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In that interview, did you say that you expected that you would not be punished at all?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never expected not to be punished at all. I never said that to anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why did you decide to tell the Prosecution this story?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why did I decide that, Mr. Karadzic? I decided that because I realised that my life had been ruined on that day. It's because of that and because of all the persons who were victims on that day. Mr. Karadzic, I was no longer thinking about my own life, not to such an extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you fire at them with the intention of destroying the Muslims as an ethnic group in Bosnia, destroying them as a people?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did any person who took part in this say anything about that intention involved? Why was this killing taking place? What were the intentions involved?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, Mr. Karadzic, who was killing with what intentions in mind. As far as I could see, some persons really enjoyed torturing others, especially when the persons from Bratunac came. I cannot explain that. I can just speak in my own name.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, I see the time, so would it be right to take the break now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll have a break for half an hour and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, I just want to make three very brief points. The mention of the other man's name was actually in public session in Popovic at transcript page 11001 and over to 11002, so there's no redaction needed in this case. The second point, to be fair to Mr. Karadzic, Mr. Erdemovic actually did mention a time of 11.00 a.m. during his testimony yesterday. And the third point was we have no objection to the plea agreement that was tendered yesterday being a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you -- so Mr. Erdemovic's comment, did it refer to the stipulation made at the Popovic trial? Transcript 11001 to 11002 --

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, that was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Oh, yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: -- giving the name of the man.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- I see. Thank you. Yes, then we will lift the confidentiality of Mr. Erdemovic's plea agreement. That will be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, I would like us to be perfectly clear, and it's probably my fault because I was not very specific in putting my questions. My question is: Did you ever stand accused of genocide?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already said, Mr. Karadzic, I cannot remember what I had been accused of in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, what I was accused of in The Hague here, and so on. If you have this document and then you could show it to me and then I could explain. Without a document or without something on paper, I cannot really say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, do you have a memory problem? You kept saying that you could not remember a great deal.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I'm not saying -- I mean, I'm not sure. I cannot say something to you and then think about whether it was correct or whether it was not correct because some statements I gave were given 15 or 16 years ago. So I cannot remember exact words and certain things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When you admitted to your guilt in your plea agreement with the OTP, did you admit to genocide as well? That can be answered with a yes or no. You should know that, shouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I really don't want to say yes or no. If you have a paper, show it to me, and then I'm going to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What did the Prosecution say to you? What would they accuse you of? What would they indict you for?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already said, Mr. Karadzic, as for these matters, the Prosecution mostly discussed them with my lawyer. I just signed this document. My lawyer was there, I was there, and Peter McCloskey I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you don't know what the essence of that agreement was, you don't know what you were indicted for, you don't know whether you were charged with genocide, whether you admitted to genocide, or was the indictment something different?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the violation of customs of war -- I cannot really explain this to you, Mr. Karadzic. I don't have this contract in front of me and I cannot tell you what this contract actually says -- no, agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But it did not say "genocide"; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, if you've got a case to put to the witness, then put it. He's already explained I think now four or perhaps five times that without a document in front of him, he has no independent recollection of the technicalities of the indictment or the agreement.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we did see the agreement, Excellency. But he - I mean the witness - for some reason seems to be evading an answer with regard to things that are perfectly clear to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, I don't think it was clear today, but I did ask you when you were at the farm and when you fired, did you shoot with the intention of destroying the Muslims as a group?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did anyone from your unit who was at the farm, who took part in this together with you, have that intention, of eradicating, exterminating the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, this has been asked and answered as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And he can't testify about what's in the mind of other people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You asked and heard the answer. Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I think in fairness to Dr. Karadzic, if he put the question did any of the people in his unit who were present with him at the farm ever state to him anything that would lead him to believe that they had the intention to destroy the Muslims as a group, I think that would be useful to get the answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Transcript page 32, lines from 11: "Q. Did you fire at them with the intention of destroying the Muslims as an ethnic group in Bosnia? "A. No. "Q. Thank you. Did any person who took part in this say anything about the intention involved? Why was this killing taking place? "A. I don't know, Mr. Karadzic, who was killing with what intentions in mind."

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think the problem was when he asked that question he was not precise as to the people in his unit who this witness had a lot of contact with as opposed to people who were generally in the area or came later in the day. So it seems to us that it would be useful to find out from the witness given the contacts he had with the people in the unit, the other seven who were participating in this, whether they ever made any statements to him that would lead him to believe that they had this intention to destroy the Muslims as a group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll allow that question to be put.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you answer, Mr. Erdemovic, can you answer what you heard?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I cannot remember, but I do not believe that we discussed who had which intention on that day and whether anyone wanted to exterminate the Muslims. We did not have such discussions. I don't remember discussing that with anyone from my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to ask you the following, Mr. Erdemovic. Did you see your unit find some gold in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you believe that in conditions of such poverty, Srebrenica or someone in Srebrenica had 12 kilogrammes of gold?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say either yes or no or whether something like that was found. I just heard these stories, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll now give you my version, Mr. Erdemovic. That gold arrived from abroad from a secret service in order to do the things that were done. What have you heard about that? What do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, before he answers the question, can we be very specific about "in order to do the things that were done," what exactly are the things that were to be done?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In order to execute people in July 1995. Did you find out or did you hear that a secret service that had contact with your detachment was the source of this gold?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You never heard about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly, but I never heard anything that resembles your story.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But did you hear that your group had contact with a French intelligence service that later took your colleagues to Zaire, and this contact was maintained for a long period of time?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have already said in the course of my testimony today, the information that a lieutenant-colonel or colonel was a contact who took individuals from my unit to Zaire - well, at the time I was in the Detention Unit, where you are now being detained - that information is information I obtained from reading the newspapers. I didn't have any contact with anyone from my unit, so I can't confirm that that is correct or not. I can't say what happened. I can't explain this to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, I want to be very clear about this. Is it Mr. Karadzic's case that these executions took place but that the 10th Sabotage Detachment was paid gold by a French intelligence service to carry out these executions? Is that the case that Mr. Karadzic is putting?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes -- just a second. Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I don't believe that this is an instance in which Dr. Karadzic has to put his case to the witness. He's questioning the credibility of the witness's account of what happened, and in the course of that, he's questioning whether or not these people were -- why -- what was the motivation for the killings, but that doesn't require him to acknowledge that the killings took place in order to put his case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But did he not himself say this is his version? I'm trying to find out.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, that's at page 37 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, page 37 --

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: -- line 20: "I'll now give you my version."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, I think Dr. Karadzic is attempting to test the witness's evidence and not necessarily commit himself to a version of events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But since he said it's his version, I think it's fair enough to ask him whether it's his case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you answer the question, Mr. Robinson or Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I -- well, I'll let Dr. Karadzic answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. [Defence counsel confer].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, I'm not claiming anything. The OTP have the burden of proof --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you specifically said: "I will now give you my version, Mr. Erdemovic. That gold arrived from abroad from a secret service in order to do the things that were done." You said this was your version. I think you need to clarify. Or you just correct your words?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't precise, Your Excellency. I want to test this witness's credibility, because in his prior testimony he mentioned the contact with the French intelligence service. He knew about the 12 kilogrammes of gold. I didn't know about that. So I wanted him to provide more details about his information that was in the framework of what he said he did. I'd like to know whether his group quarrelled about the gold, whether they had contact with a secret service or not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, the Chamber has never prohibited you from testing the credibility of a witness, but be precise in putting your case. You said it was your case. There's a lot of difference.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise for being imprecise. My question for Mr. Erdemovic was as follows: What does he know about that? What did he hear about that and what does he know for sure about the contact with the secret service and about where the gold came from, since he didn't observe this gold being found in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I think he answered the question in any event. I think your time is almost up. How much longer would you need, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You have five minutes to conclude.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Excellency. I believe that will be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, you testified on numerous occasions and there is much that is contradictory. Did you act in this way on purpose and why? Today we heard that you deliberately provided false information on dates. So were you doing this on purpose, providing contradictory information in the statements that you gave?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So we -- you were asked about the dates. Yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: The first part of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: -- was just argumentative and a statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You need to be specific in putting the questions. But, Mr. Erdemovic, the question about the date, can you answer the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. As I have already said, when I gave my statement to the journalist in Novi Sad, this journalist was an ABC journalist. Kremenovic and I spoke to each other and we said it would be good to provide her with the wrong dates. If something happened, it wouldn't be possible to prove things if, for example, we were arrested or something like that. But as I have already said, the journalist was searched, first of all, in Belgrade, the tapes with my statements disappeared from her bag. And when we were in -- when I was in court in Novi Sad, the investigating judge who was examining me on that day -- I gave him the same dates, but in fact they already had all that information.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. I have no further questions. I could put other questions, but I don't want to move into other areas. I could start enumerating the inconsistencies I have noticed, but I won't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Mitchell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, I have only one area that I briefly want to ask you about. Earlier today at page 26 of the transcript it was suggested to you that Pelemis took a Muslim man out of prison and ordered that he be killed and that it was only after you had seen footage of the body in Srebrenica that you said that Pelemis had ordered the killing of the man in the American army jacket. I just want to ask you a couple of questions about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can I have 65 ter 8943 in e-court. While this is coming up, Mr. President, I can represent that we - the Office of the Prosecutor - received that footage on the 27th of March, 2009.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: This is a transcript of an interview on the 24th of April, 1996, between you, Mr. Erdemovic, and Mr. Ruez and Mr. Nicholson from the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: If we can go to page 14 in English, page 10 in the B/C/S. And the relevant part in English starts about halfway down the page. We can scroll down in the B/C/S as well. And if we can go over to the next page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And my question is: Mr. Erdemovic, is this, what you're describing here in your interview of April 1996, is this what we saw on the footage that you were shown yesterday of the same man in the green jacket in the middle of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the statement about that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Can we now go to page 20 in the English and 13 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Right at the top of the page you again describe the killing of a Muslim man. If you can just read that.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: I just want you to read this and then let us know when you finish reading this section.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: And my question is: Mr. Erdemovic, is this, the killing of the Muslim man described here, is this the same man who Zoran killed in the centre of town and who we saw on the footage; or is this a different killing that you're describing here?

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This man is a different person who was in detention in Vlasenica. It's not the same person who Zoran killed in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Erdemovic. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In answering Mr. Karadzic's question about the -- taking a man from -- out of prison and killing him, you said you did not attribute that to Mr. Pelemis. Are we talking about a different event? I'm a bit confused about this. It's -- on page 26 -- you referred to transcript page 26.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. President, this might be something that's best clarified with the witness. I can explain it or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, could you do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: My understanding is we're talking about two completely different incidents. There's one in the centre of town, on the 11th of July --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure I am hearing your voice. Could you repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: We're talking about two completely different incidents, one that occurs on the 11th of July in the centre of Srebrenica, where a man has his throat slit by Zoran; and then there's a completely separate incident, where Pelemis orders that a man be taken out of prison in Vlasenica and killed in the same way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you have transcript page 26 in front --

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Question from line 5 -- and then in answer to that question he said -- Mr. Erdemovic said he didn't attribute that to Mr. Pelemis. So I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: That's something that I think needs to be clarified with him, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MITCHELL
utterances.text: Mr. Erdemovic, earlier today when you were asked about the killing of the man who was taken out from the prison in Vlasenica you said: "I did not attribute that to Mr. Pelemis. I said that Pecanac was involved in this, as far as I can recall." You said: "As for this man in Srebrenica whose throat had been slit by Zoran Maljic, I know for certain that that was ordered by Pelemis." Now, if you look at your interview of April 1996, you say: "As far as I know, Pelemis had promised that he," that is, the Muslim man, "would be left alive because he was -- he had been helping our unit, but on the morning of the 13th he ordered two men to kill him." So can you explain, in your interview of 1996 you referred to Pelemis and today you said as far as you could recall Pecanac was involved in this.

utterances.speaker: DRAZEN ERDEMOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think I can explain this. That evening when we returned to Vlasenica from Srebrenica, it was late at night and Major Pecanac was already there.
